items.title: Are Drone Ports the Next Annoying Tech Neighbor?
items.summary: Rick and Marcia LeCompte loved to watch the Cooper’s hawks that frequented a sweet-gum tree in their yard in Baton Rouge, La. But this October, the hawks were gone. Marcia LeCompte is convinced the birds were scared away by the same flying robots that have been vexing the couple since early September. The noise had them spending less time outside in their garden, and even inside their home, they couldn’t escape the near-constant buzzing. Angry and feeling harassed, the LeComptes began to think about moving. The problem: delivery drones. Amazon’s MK30 delivery drones are large and must fly near the ground when making deliveries. Annabel Lee-Ellis/Press Association/AP Images Last August, Amazon Prime Air began flying its MK30 drones from a distribution center 3.2 kilometers (2 miles) from the LeComptes’ home.
